note: Prognostic and diagnostic-risk markers in AL amyloidosis, including laboratory and imaging measures, not yet validated for clinical decisions. Selected from peer-reviewed papers that test the marker in more than one cohort or bring a clearly new approach; single-cohort correlations with older methods are not listed.
scope: This list belongs to the AL amyloidosis topic only.

items.n: Monoclonal light chain N-glycosylation on MASS-FIX
items.why: A feature of the light chain itself, seen on routine MASS-FIX testing, that may flag the monoclonal gammopathies likely to become AL amyloidosis, before organ damage.
items.cohort: 414 people with MGUS from the Olmsted County screening cohort, followed for a median of 22.2 years (Dispenzieri 2020); 6,315 patients tested with MASS-FIX in routine practice at the Mayo Clinic (Mellors 2021); light chain sequences from 220 patients with AL amyloidosis or myeloma followed at the authors' centres in Italy, with published sequences (Nevone 2022).
items.data: Glycosylated light chains in 6% of MGUS. 20-year progression to a malignant plasma cell disorder 67% vs 13% with vs without glycosylation, and to AL amyloidosis 21% vs 3%. In routine testing, glycosylation (5% of positive samples) was more common in AL amyloidosis, cold agglutinin disease, κ light chains and IgM. In κ light chains from AL amyloidosis, most glycosylation sites lay in framework region 3.
items.adj: Progression risk was independent of the Mayo MGUS risk score; not adjusted for other factors in the abstracts.
items.missing: Progression risk was measured in one cohort with few events; no study has tested whether screening glycosylated MGUS with cardiac and renal biomarkers leads to earlier diagnosis.
items.status: MASS-FIX is a clinical test at some laboratories; using glycosylation to decide follow-up is research use.

items.n: Free light chain mass spectrometry (FLC-MS) negativity after treatment
items.why: A blood test more sensitive than the free light chain assay, which separates complete responses with and without a detectable amyloidogenic light chain, without a marrow sample.
items.cohort: 487 patients with AL amyloidosis at the Mayo Clinic, with serum tested at diagnosis and 6 and 12 months after treatment.
items.data: Light chain isotype by FLC-MS matched the fibril type in all patients. FLC-MS negative at 12 months: 20.7% of all patients and 39% of those in conventional complete response. In complete response at 12 months, median OS not reached if FLC-MS negative vs 108 months if positive (P=0.024); cardiac response 70% vs 50% (P=0.015). FLC-MS negativity at 12 months was independent in multivariable analysis.
items.adj: Multivariable analysis reported; the factors included are not listed in the abstract.
items.missing: One centre and one assay; no independent cohort, no comparison with marrow MRD in the same patients, and no trial that changes treatment by FLC-MS.
